title: The Seventh and Eighth Ranks
subtitle: Converging Attacks, Blind Pigs, and Turning Movements
summary: Mastering the ultimate fruits of open-file invasion: sweeping the enemy pawns, executing mating nets with doubled rooks, and turning movements.
aphorism: A rook on the 7th rank is an absolute tyrant. Two rooks on the 7th are the infamous 'blind pigs' — devouring everything in sight.
attribution: 100th Anniversary Centenary Edition. Based directly on Aron Nimzowitsch's My System (1925), Part I, Chapter 3.

body.historicalContext: Nimzowitsch categorized every type of 7th-rank assault with scientific precision, demonstrating why even a heavy material deficit is easily overcome when you command doubled rooks on the 7th rank.

sections.title: Converging & Revolutionary Attacks on the 7th
sections.markdown:
Once a rook seizes the **[[seventh-rank|seventh rank]]**, you must select a specific target of attack (Diagram 67 in *My System*).

White doubles rooks on the 7th rank with **1.Rdd7!**. The two rooks coordinate against the f7 and c7 targets. If Black's f7 pawn advances or falls, White's rooks sweep laterally across the rank like a scythe, devouring all enemy pawns from the flank.

moves.comment: White invades with the second rook, doubling on the 7th rank!
Black tries to mobilize the king rook.
The doubled rooks break through on the 7th rank.

sections.title: The 'Blind Pigs' (Doubled Rooks on the 7th)
sections.markdown:
When two rooks occupy the seventh rank together, chess lore calls them the **'blind pigs'** (Diagram 76 in *My System*).

Like hungry beasts, they devour pawns and weave inescapable mating nets. Here White delivers the crushing blow with **1.Rg7+ Kh8 2.Rxh7+ Kg8 3.Reg7#**!

moves.comment: First check: driving the king into the corner.
Black's king is forced to h8.
Devouring the h7 pawn with check!

sections.title: The 'Absolute' 7th Rank & Passed Pawns
sections.markdown:
By the **'absolute' 7th rank**, Nimzowitsch meant a rook on the 7th that completely traps the enemy king on the 8th rank (Diagram 74).

When combined with a far-advanced passed pawn, the absolute 7th rank wins by force. White plays **1.b7!**, and Black is completely powerless to prevent the winning manoeuvre **Re7–c7–c8+**!

moves.comment: The passed pawn advances to the 7th rank!
Black puts the rook behind the pawn.
White transfers the rook to c7, preparing Rc8 to queen the pawn.
Black's king tries to flee the corner.
Decisive pin! The pawn will promote next move.

engineLens.takeaway: Stockfish confirms that the combination of the absolute 7th rank and a 7th-rank passed pawn is decisive in all variations.

drills.title: Invade the Seventh
drills.markdown: White already has one rook on c7. Bring your second rook from d1 to d7 to double on the seventh rank.

hints.text: Move the d1 rook to d7 to double on the 7th rank.

feedback.correct: Splendid! 1.Rdd7 establishes the dominant doubled rooks on the 7th rank.
feedback.wrong: Play Rdd7 to double rooks on the 7th rank.

drills.title: Trigger the Blind Pigs
drills.markdown: White has doubled rooks on the 7th rank. Deliver the checking blow on g7 to dismantle Black's defense.

feedback.correct: Brilliant! 1.Rg7+ drives the king into the mating net.
